title: Turn Your CLI Tool Into a Shareable Web App

sections.content:
## What You'll Build

You built a text summarizer CLI in lesson 11-8. In this lesson you'll wrap it in a web interface — a simple HTML form anyone can visit in a browser — and deploy it to Railway so it's live on the internet with a permanent URL you can share.

This is the bridge between "I built a tool for myself" and "I built a tool others can use."

**Why web UI matters:** A CLI tool requires someone to have Node.js installed and know how to use a terminal. A web app requires a browser. Going from CLI to web UI expands your potential users from ~100 people (technical) to billions (anyone with a phone). The code change is smaller than you think.

## The Architecture

Your CLI tool reads text from a file and calls the Anthropic API. The web version does the same thing, but instead of reading from a file, it reads from an HTML form.

**CLI flow:**
```
User → terminal command → reads file → Anthropic API → prints to terminal
```

**Web flow:**
```
User → browser form → Express server → Anthropic API → HTML response in browser
```

The Anthropic API call is identical. You're adding:
1. An Express.js server (handles HTTP requests)
2. An HTML form (the user interface)
3. A route that connects the form to your existing summarization logic

**Express.js** is a minimal Node.js web framework — the most widely used in the world. It handles the HTTP plumbing so you can focus on the application logic.

sections.title: Build and Deploy Your Web App
sections.content:
Take your summarizer from CLI to a live web app on the internet.

---

## Phase 1 — Build the Web Server Locally (20 min)

**Step 1 — Set up the project:**
Open your summarizer project from lesson 11-8 in VS Code and launch Claude Code:
```
claude
```

**Step 2 — Ask Claude Code to add the web layer:**
```
I have a CLI text summarizer that uses the Anthropic API (see summarize.js).
Add a web interface to this project:

1. Install Express.js
2. Create server.js with:
   - A GET / route that shows an HTML form with a textarea
   - A POST /summarize route that takes the form text, calls Anthropic,
     returns the summary in a styled HTML page
   - Clean, minimal styling inline
   - Error handling that shows a user-friendly message
3. The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY should come from process.env (not hardcoded)
4. PORT should come from process.env with fallback to 3000

Use the same summarization logic from summarize.js.
```

**Step 3 — Test locally:**
```
node server.js
```
Open http://localhost:3000, paste some text, click Summarize. Does it work?

**Step 4 — Improve the UI:** Ask Claude Code:
- "Add a character counter that shows how many characters are in the textarea"
- "Show a loading spinner while the summary is being generated"
- "Add a 'Copy summary' button to the results page"

Each of these makes the app genuinely more usable.

---

## Phase 2 — Deploy to Railway (20 min)

Railway is the simplest free platform for deploying Node.js apps with environment variables.

**Step 1 — Sign up at railway.app** (use GitHub sign in)

**Step 2 — Push your code to GitHub first:**
Ask Claude Code: "Create a .gitignore that excludes node_modules and .env. Then help me push this project to a new GitHub repo called 'ai-summarizer'."

**Step 3 — Deploy to Railway:**
1. In Railway dashboard, click **New Project**
2. Select **Deploy from GitHub repo**
3. Pick your `ai-summarizer` repo
4. Railway detects Node.js automatically and starts deploying

**Step 4 — Add your API key:**
1. In Railway, go to your service → **Variables**
2. Add: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` = your API key
3. Railway restarts the deployment with the variable available

**Step 5 — Get your URL:**
In Railway: Settings → Generate Domain → copy the `*.railway.app` URL

Open it in your browser. Test it. Share the URL.

---

## Phase 3 — Make It Better (15 min)

Ask Claude Code to add at least one of:

**Rate limiting:** "Add rate limiting so one IP can only make 5 summarize requests per hour."

**Word count stats:** "Before showing the summary, show the original text's word count and estimated reading time."

**Different summary styles:** "Add a dropdown on the form: Bullet points, Short paragraph (50 words), Detailed (200 words). Pass the selected style to the API prompt."

**Text length limit:** "If the pasted text is over 10,000 characters, show a warning that only the first 10,000 characters will be summarised."

Push changes to GitHub — Railway auto-deploys on every push.

sections.title: Workshop A — Add Authentication to Your Web App
sections.content:
Add a simple password gate to your web app so only people you share the password with can use it.

This is not enterprise authentication — it's a quick gate for a personal tool. Good enough for sharing with a small group.

**Step 1 — Ask Claude Code:**
```
Add simple password protection to my Express web app.
Implement it with a cookie-based session:
- A login page (/login) with a password form
- If password matches the PASSWORD environment variable, set a session cookie and redirect to /
- All other routes check for the session cookie — if missing, redirect to /login
- A /logout route that clears the cookie

Use express-session for session management.
```

**Step 2 — Add the PASSWORD variable in Railway:**
Go to Variables → add `PASSWORD` = a strong password of your choice

**Step 3 — Test:** Open your Railway URL. Does it redirect to /login? After logging in, can you use the summarizer? Does /logout work?

**Step 4 — Share with 2 people.** Give them the URL and password. Can they use it on their devices?

sections.title: Workshop B — Build a Different AI Web Tool
sections.content:
Apply the Express + Anthropic pattern to build a different AI tool of your choice.

**Step 1 — Choose a tool to build:** Ideas:
- **Writing improver:** paste text, choose improvement type (clarity/tone/grammar), get improved version
- **Email subject line generator:** paste email body, get 5 subject line options
- **Code explainer:** paste code, Claude explains it in plain English
- **Meeting notes formatter:** paste raw notes, get a structured summary with action items
- **Headline generator:** paste article, get 5 headline options

**Step 2 — Ask Claude Code to build the full web app:**
```
Build an Express.js web app that does [your chosen tool].

UI: [describe the form inputs — what does the user provide?]
AI processing: [describe what Claude should do with the input]
Output: [what does the user see — formatted text, list, comparison?]

Requirements:
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from environment variable
- PORT from environment variable (fallback 3000)
- Clean, minimal UI
- Loading state while API call is in progress
- Error handling
```

**Step 3 — Test locally, then deploy to Railway.**

**Step 4 — Share and get feedback.** Ask 3 people to try it. What confused them? What would they use it for?

sections.question: Your web app is live on Railway. A user pastes a 50,000-word document. The Anthropic API call fails with 'max_tokens exceeded'. What should you do?
options: Show an error and ask the user to paste less text
Truncate input to a sensible limit on the server, warn the user, and process the truncated version — never let raw user input reach the API without validation
sections.explanation: Always validate and limit user input on the server before sending it to an external API. A 50,000-word document would exceed context limits and cost significantly more than intended. The correct approach: check input length on the server, if it exceeds your limit (e.g., 5,000 words) either reject it with a clear message or truncate with a warning. This protects your API budget, prevents errors, and gives users feedback about what your tool can handle. Never pass raw user input to an API without bounds checking.

sections.content: **Lesson 11-10 complete.** You've bridged the gap between a local tool and a deployed web application. Everything you build with the Anthropic API can become a web tool someone else can use — the pattern is always the same: Express server + form + API call + response page. Next: running AI locally with Ollama.
